title: Google’s AI Chip Push Lifts Cloud Sales but Squeezes Cash Flow
gist: Reuters (reposted on SemiWiki) reports Alphabet's external TPU sales made a meaningful contribution as Google Cloud revenue more than doubled in the September quarter, but building unsold TPU inventory is draining cash. Shares fell nearly 11% after another quarter of cash burn and guidance for sharply higher AI infrastructure spend; TPU sales are expected to ramp significantly in 2027.

insights.claim: Alphabet is now making billions selling homegrown TPU AI chips it once reserved for internal use, competing with Nvidia.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Google is emerging as a merchant AI-accelerator competitor to Nvidia.
insights.quote: Alphabet is making billions of dollars selling homegrown AI chips it once reserved for internal use

insights.claim: Alphabet said TPU sales made a meaningful contribution as Google Cloud revenue more than doubled in the September quarter, though it does not break out TPU revenue or margins.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: TPU is a key driver of Cloud hypergrowth but unquantified, limiting visibility.
insights.locator: Alphabet does not break out revenue

insights.claim: Google Cloud chief Thomas Kurian said TPU system sales, bundling chips with networking, storage and software, will rise further in the current quarter and ramp significantly in 2027.
insights.speaker: Thomas Kurian
insights.so_what: Sets up a 2027 TPU revenue inflection for Alphabet and competitive pressure on Nvidia.

insights.claim: Alphabet last year agreed to supply Anthropic with TPUs worth tens of billions of dollars, and media reports say it is in talks on a similar deal with OpenAI.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Frontier-lab anchor customers validate TPU as an Nvidia alternative.

insights.claim: Selling TPUs requires Alphabet to spend on hardware well before customers pay, so unsold TPU systems now appear in inventory and drain cash in a different cycle from traditional capex, per CFO Anat Ashkenazi.
insights.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi
insights.so_what: Hardware business model shifts Alphabet's FCF profile toward working-capital intensity.
insights.quote: it’s not the traditional kind of capex but rather a different cycle of cash flow generation

insights.claim: Alphabet shares fell nearly 11% after it reported another quarter of cash burn and reiterated that AI infrastructure spending would rise sharply next year.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Market is penalizing AI capex and working-capital drag despite revenue growth.
insights.quote: Its shares fell nearly 11% on Thursday after the company reported another quarter of cash burn

insights.claim: Check Capital's Jeremy Saltzberg calls the cash pressure short-term gyrations and expects TPU margins to be not significantly different from Nvidia GPU margins.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Saltzberg
insights.so_what: Bull case: the selloff mis-prices a potentially Nvidia-like margin business.
insights.quote: We completely think these are short-term gyrations
